title: Existence of normalized tensor-Hom models
statement: Fix universes $d,t,u$, a prime $\ell$, a field $E$ finite-dimensional over $\mathbf Q_\ell$, a scheme $Y$ in universe $t$, a finite-field datum $D$ of characteristic $p$ in universe $d$, and $\ell\ne p$. On the small pro-etale site of $Y$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $B=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$ and $B_n=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^{n+1})_Y$ be the coefficient sheaves [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Work in the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(B)$ and $D(B_n)$ of module sheaves at coefficient universe $\max(u,t+1)$. Write $H_B,H_{B_n}$ for the recorded derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], $F_n:D(B)\to D(B_n)$ for derived reduction [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction], and $Q$ for complex localization. There exists a tensor presentation $a$ for $B$ [def-sf-integral-hom-reduction-models] such that for every $n\ge0$ there is a reduction presentation from $a$ at level $n$. This is the existence of the ordinary uncompleted tensor, its evaluation-normalized adjunction, and the normalized coefficient tensor comparison; it asserts no Hom comparison invertibility and no completeness preservation.

proof.text: The tensor presentation exists by the normalized K-flat tensor construction.
For every fixed n, the same source presentation admits a normalized reduction presentation by ordinary scalar extension and the derived universal property.
